findings.title: traceID dropped from request log; contextual logger may not add it
findings.body: The old logRequest explicitly appended traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext, and also pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName and dsUID. The new code relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx) to supply these. The contextual attributes cover only endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname. traceID is not added by the ContextualLoggerMiddleware. It is only present if the infra logger's FromContext adds it, which is not shown here. If it does not, the 'Plugin Request Completed' logs lose traceID, which breaks log-to-trace correlation. No test covers this.

findings.title: FromContext fallback discards the context
findings.body: If the type assertion fails, the code returns d.New(), which drops the contextual attributes and does not contain the requested context. The failure is silent. Callers such as the logger middleware then lose pluginId, endpoint and the other attributes without any signal. It would be better to fall back to d, or to wrap the returned logger.

findings.title: Logger name still says instrumentation
findings.body: The PR renames instrumentation to metrics, but the logger is still created as log.New("plugin.instrumentation"). The name is now inconsistent with the new middleware names. It is also unclear whether it was intentionally left unchanged to keep the log name stable.

findings.title: No tests for new ContextualLoggerMiddleware
findings.body: The new middleware moves behavior that previously lived in the instrumentation middleware: context enrichment with the contextual logger. No test verifies that it sets the attributes, or that the LoggerMiddleware picks them up. The helper is also still named instrumentContext despite the rename.
